description:
kith-peer/src/lib.rs lines 1007-1031: build_peer_deliver_request() takes 9 positional string arguments (message_id, chat_id, sender_user_id, body, body_type, sent_at, reply_to, attachments, broadcast_mentions) with no type differentiation between them. All string arguments are &str, making it trivial to accidentally swap e.g. body and body_type, or message_id and chat_id, with no compile error.

There is also build_peer_deliver_request_full() (line 1034) which adds a PeerDeliverRequestParams struct for the remaining optional fields — the right pattern — but the required fields are still positional.

This is a defensive-code-forcing issue: every call site must independently verify argument order. A unit test that passes wrong arguments in the wrong order will produce a valid JSON object (all are strings) that only fails at the receiving peer's validation layer, potentially much later.

The crate already uses the params-struct pattern (OutboundMessageParams in kith-store, PeerDeliverRequestParams in kith-peer) for optional fields. The same pattern should apply to the required fields.

Fix: introduce a PeerDeliverRequiredParams struct (or merge into PeerDeliverRequestParams) that names all required fields, and change build_peer_deliver_request_full() to accept it. Remove build_peer_deliver_request() as a separate function or make it a method on the params struct.
title: kith-peer: build_peer_deliver_request has 9-argument positional signature
